newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains forced lower by sterling strength.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains forced lower by sterling strength.

text.p: LIFFE wheat was forced down by the strength of sterling, although it did manage to close off lows as the currency came off its highest levels against the German mark, traders said.
January 1998 was most active, with 123 of the total 380 lots. It last traded 0.60 stg down, at 84.15 stg, compared with a low of 83.75 stg.

One trader pronounced himself pleased with the market's performance, in view of the strength of the currency. "The question now is where you find the fresh sellers from," he said. He expected to see some recovery on Tuesday if sterling were to ease overnight.
Barley also fell. Of a total 85 lots done, 50 were on November, which last traded 0.75 stg lower at 78.50 stg.
The currency's rise also hit the delivered market, with feed wheat for Norfolk/Suffolk in July done at 80.00 stg, compared with 83.00 stg on Friday.
